Awards[edit]

AIME Qualification[edit]

Pre-2020[edit]

At least the top 2.5% of scorers on the AMC 10 and the top 5% of scorers on the AMC 12 were invited to participate in the AIME.

2020-2025[edit]

Since 2020, the AIME qualification threshold has been adjusted to allow a consistent number of students (usually 6000–7000) to qualify each year, rather than relying on fixed percentages. Still, at least the top 2.5% of AMC 10 participants and top 5% of AMC 12 participants are guaranteed to qualify for AIME. As of August 2025, international students will no longer affect AIME cutoffs. In addition, the limit of 120 for the AMC 10 and 100 for the AMC 12 does not exist anymore, so theoretically, the cutoffs could go up to 150.

Post-2025[edit]

Since 2026, the AIME qualification threshold has been fixed at 85 points for the AMC 12 and 100 points for the AMC 10 regardless of distribution.

Honor Rolls[edit]

Since 2020 MAA documents use inconsistent terminology for the honor rolls.

2025 award certificate templates can be seen here (as of December 2025):

  • AMC 8 Templates
  • AMC 10 Templates
  • AMC 12 Templates

"HR" 5% Honor Roll[edit]

As of 2025, MAA Report page does not name this honor roll. Printed certificates read "Certificate of Distinction" for the AMC 10 and AMC 12 and "Honor Roll" for the AMC 8.

Awarded to the top 5% of scorers on the AMC 8, AMC 10, and AMC 12, respectively.

Informally, the term "Honor Roll" or "HR" refers to this Top 5% Score honor roll.

"DHR" 1% Distinguished Honor Roll / Honor Roll of Distinction[edit]

As of 2025, MAA Report page calls this "Distinguished Honor Roll". Printed certificates read "Honor Roll of Distinction for scoring in the top 1%

Awarded to the top 1% of scorers on the AMC 8, AMC 10, and AMC 12, respectively.

Informally, the term "DHR" refers this Top 1% Score honor roll.

Achievement Roll[edit]

  • Awarded to students in 6th grade or lower who score 15 points or higher on the AMC 8.
  • Awarded to students in 8th grade or lower who score 90 points or higher on the AMC 10.
  • Awarded to students in 10th grade or lower who score 90 points or higher on the AMC 12.

USAMO/USAJMO Qualification[edit]

From the 2026-2027 school year and onwards: USAMO/USAJMO qualification will be solely determined by AIME Score

Since 2025-2026 school year: USAMO/USAJMO qualifying index is equal to (AIME score multiplied by 20) + (AMC score). This index score is used to determine qualification for USAMO/USAJMO.

2024-2025 and earlier school years: USAMO/USAJMO qualifying index is equal to (AIME score multiplied by 10) + (AMC score.)

Index values that are greater-than or equal to the cutoff scores qualify for USAMO/USAJMO.

  • AMC 12 scores are used for USAMO qualification.
  • AMC 10 scores are used for USAJMO qualification.

Reportedly, AMC 12 students near the USAMO cutoff have qualified for the USAJMO in 2025, although it is unclear whether this will be a continuing practice.
